## Owner statements 2026-10-09 — every source is scanned for every parameter; the parameter list is seeded from the existing terms; the catalogue plan, its critique and its tooling

Given in the session https://claude.ai/code/session_01DYqutJg8mWCGUQvqKzqAeM and recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Each statement is quoted verbatim beside what it answered; times are UTC. The questions are in `scratchpad/session_2026-10-09-research-batch-24-parameter-pilot/catalogue-plan-v2.md` section 2.5 and its addenda. The session record is `sessions/session_2026-10-09-research-batch-24-parameter-pilot.md`.

**The method**, stated unprompted (02:35):

> "note that while we search by slug, we scan each source for any and all applicable parameters. we may need to just prepopulate a parameters list."

and, when commissioning the critique of the catalogue plan and its rewrite (20:22), the whole message:

> "Perform Fable 5.1 read-only adversarial critique of the above. Interrogate quality, logic, sequencing and flexibility of pipeline all directions as well as all gates, reads, writes, conditionals. Ensure that all of our terms/parameters in catalogued will be leveraged in such a way where we can scrape information across any parameter if it appears in any source no matter the slug. Slugs guide our searches, but they do not guide what we derive and mine from sources! Our terms/parameter catalogue will, which means I expect harvesting across multiple terms if a source discusses multiple terms. Ensure that we can add and expand parameter catalogue as required based on new information we come across. Pass off to Opus to rewrite plan judiciously and exhaustively."

**Answers to the session's questions**, in order:

- "Is the existing `terms` registry acceptable as the seed for the parameter list?" — "1 yes" (03:08).
- "Does a `preliminary` or `skim` extraction ever govern a published cell?" — "2 ..yes? like, one pulled from another slug? should be yes, but we still tag it for follow up later" (03:08). This was ambiguous between a skimmed figure and a figure from another slug; D1 below resolved it.
- "WP12: confirm the R7 floor removal?" — "3 don't know what is" (03:08), then, after a plain-words restatement, "keep wp12 rule" (05:48). The R7 floor stays removed and R5 stays re-aimed at admitted sources.
- "populate a parameters table" (05:48), then, typed mid-turn, "we need like the 90+ cleaned parameters without values" (05:52).
- "A. The 94 existing terms. I would turn each object into its measurable quantity ... and propose the new names for your review. B. The 93 old guidebook items with the numbers stripped ..." — "A" (06:01). The session then found that parameter names may not be invented (the 2026-09-09 ruling above), so A could not be carried out as offered.
- "... why would you develop a parameter database for coverage of all accessible design terms possible by using batch 23 that came from a specific slug" (06:06). The session withdrew the batch 23 scan.
- "pull from the major codes, literature and advocacy from major countries" (queued 06:07:12, before the session's "1. slug by slug / 2. you seed it" options arrived at 06:07:27, so that choice was never answered) and, typed mid-turn, "there should be an exhaustive bibliography that is outdated but correct that has info on each jurisdiction code bodies and major groups".
- After the plan was rewritten: "D1: yes figure from source filed by another slug allowed. skimmed values are not publishable" (21:17), and then, later the same evening, "D2 yes, D3 keep the rule, D8 approve tooling".
- Immediately after, on D3: "D3 for parameter terms? it can be pulled from previous catalogues of entries for prepopulating". It qualifies "keep the rule" and is read in item 3 below.
- Asked which previous catalogues D3 meant, what guard applies to names taken from them, and whether a second branch may carry the first tooling pull request, the owner selected (from listed options, not typed): the catalogues **"Code and standards registries"** and **"Old corpus terms"** (the old Part 4 item names were offered and NOT selected); the guard **"Screen, then you approve"**; and **"Yes, second branch"**.

**What these establish**

1. **The scan contract.** Every admitted source is read against the whole parameter list, whatever slug it was filed under. Slugs plan and log searches; they do not decide what is taken from a source. One source can yield many parameters. Arguments and qualitative findings are mined as well as figures (the 2026-09-18 ruling in `sessions/session_2026-09-18-research-batch-15-t2-synthesis-threshold.md` is the root).
2. **The seed.** The parameter list is seeded from the existing terms registry. Parameters 4 to 12 (corridor width, turning circle, operating force, reverberation time, LRV contrast, door width, colour temperature, headroom clearance, ramp run length), added on this branch by commit `a8b7c11`, are kept, not reverted, and go to `main` through a pull request (D2).
3. **Names.** The 2026-09-09 rule stands for names that come out of research (D3, "keep the rule"): a name is minted only from a phrase an admitted source uses, through `db.py add-term --from-observation`, never by hand and never bearing a value. For prepopulating the parameter list the owner then permitted names "pulled from previous catalogues of entries", and selected which: the code and standards registries (`references/standards-registry.md`, `references/tier456-verified-sources.json`, `references/co1-verified-sources.json`, `references/co2-verified-sources.json`) and the terms of the pre-reset corpus (`_archived/data/corpus-pre-reset-2026-08-06.db`). The old Part 4 item names are not a permitted source. The guard is "Screen, then you approve": every candidate name is screened (no digit, comparator or min/max word, no old item code) and listed in one table, with the catalogue and the entry it came from, for the owner to approve before any is minted. Minting a name on this authority needs a route `insert_term` does not have. The session proposed that route as an addition to tooling T1 (`catalogue-plan-v2.md` Addenda 3 and 4); D8 predates it, so the owner's approval of T1 (item 5) does not cover its design, which goes to the owner on the T1 pull request. This narrows the "never by hand" clause for prepopulation only. The back-pointer grammar cannot mark the 2026-09-09 clause because it sits in this ledger (see item 6); this item is the mark.
4. **Cross-slug figures and skimmed figures (D1).** A figure taken from a source filed under another slug may be extracted and may set a published value, tagged for follow-up (the 03:08 words were not withdrawn). The owner's words are "skimmed values are not publishable". [ASSUMPTION: "skimmed" means a figure whose `extraction_method` is `skim`, and the determination engine is to leave such figures out of what sets a value. The owner named neither the column nor the engine rule; this reading is the session's, from `catalogue-plan-v2.md` Addendum 1, and stands until the owner confirms or corrects it.] Whether a figure read in full but still marked `preliminary` may set a value is NOT settled (D1c) and is not changed by this entry.
5. **Tooling.** D8 approved the first tooling pull request as `catalogue-plan-v2.md` section 4.2 items 1 to 5. It ships as its own pull request, on its own branch, and merges before this branch's pull request (`CLAUDE.md` rule 10); the second to merge takes `main`'s `data/guidebook.db` and re-runs `python3 scripts/migrate_db.py`. What T1 carries beyond those items (the catalogue minting route of item 3, and any change the session built to meet D1) was not shown to the owner before it was built, and is for the owner to accept or strike on the T1 pull request.
6. **The critique was commissioned by the owner.** The owner commissioned a read-only adversarial critique of the catalogue plan, saved verbatim in `scratchpad/session_2026-10-09-research-batch-24-parameter-pilot/catalogue-plan-critique-fable.md`. That supersedes, for that plan only, the 2026-08-19 clause that plans, critiques and handoffs are not adversarial-pass subjects. The back-pointer grammar below cannot mark that clause: it sits in this ledger, and the audit counts a target quote in the target file's raw text, where the SUPERSEDES line itself would make a second copy. This paragraph is the mark.
7. **The pilot's scope.** The batch 24 pilot in `process-gap-remediation-plan.md` section 7 is superseded in the places marked below. The pilot's scope, a judgement-stage re-read of batch 23's fourteen sources, is replaced by the scan contract above. Observation is no longer limited to phrases that carry a figure: arguments, qualitative findings and every quantity a source treats as a design quantity are observed. The pilot's budget of new parameters was exceeded on the owner's direction ("populate a parameters table", then D2 kept the nine promoted) and is superseded to that extent. **The pilot's cap on extractions (twice batch 23's) is not superseded:** no owner words address it. It budgets a pilot whose scope is replaced, so it has nothing to bind until a batch is run to the scan contract; whether any cap carries over, and whether the review unit is one source (`catalogue-plan-v2.md` section 1.1, F16, the session's own recommendation), is put to the owner.

```
SUPERSEDES: scratchpad/session_2026-10-01-research-batch-23/process-gap-remediation-plan.md :: "The pilot is a judgement-stage re-read of batch 23's 14 admitted sources."
  BY: references/project-standards.md :: "is replaced by the scan contract above"
SUPERSEDES: scratchpad/session_2026-10-01-research-batch-23/process-gap-remediation-plan.md :: "New parameters ≤ 4."
  BY: references/project-standards.md :: "is superseded to that extent"
SUPERSEDES: scratchpad/session_2026-10-01-research-batch-23/process-gap-remediation-plan.md :: "Do this for every concept phrase the source states a figure for"
  BY: references/project-standards.md :: "Observation is no longer limited to phrases that carry a figure"
```

**Not yet answered**, so nothing here approves them: D4 (exhaustion judged per parameter and jurisdiction), D5 (who reviews vocabulary in bulk), D6 (an item is one parameter), D7 (the category list), D9 (publish Release 0), D10 (read what is held before fetching), D11 (read out-of-bucket sources already held), D12 (this entry, which `CLAUDE.md` rule 0 requires regardless), D13 (the two finished batch 23 scans as test material), and whether the pilot's extraction cap carries over to the scan contract. The recommendations in `catalogue-plan-v2.md` section 10 stand unapproved. The batch 23 scan outputs are not data.

CONDITION: any session asking how a source is scanned, whether a figure from another slug may be used or a skimmed one published, on whose authority parameters 4 to 12 exist, whether a parameter name may be minted by hand, from an observed phrase, or from a registry or the pre-reset corpus, whether the pilot's scope or row budgets still bind, or whether a plan may be critiqued.
ACTION: (1) Scan every admitted source for every parameter in the catalogue; never limit a reading to the slug a source was filed under. (2) Take names from observed phrases; mint nothing by hand. For prepopulation the owner permits names from the code and standards registries and the pre-reset corpus terms (never the old Part 4 item names), screened and approved in one table before any is minted. (3) Treat a skimmed figure as not publishable; treat a cross-slug figure as allowed and tagged. (4) Build the first tooling pull request as its own pull request, on its own branch off `main`, before any bulk promotion. (5) Do not read the pilot's scope, its new-parameter budget or its figure-only step as binding. Its cap on extractions is NOT lifted: ask the owner whether it carries over to the scan contract, and treat the one-source review unit as a recommendation, not a ruling. (6) A critique of a plan needs the owner's fresh commission; this one covered the catalogue plan only.

-- 102_observation_per_sighting.sql
-- SCHEMA migration — an observation is ONE SIGHTING: a phrase AT A PLACE in a source.
-- Tooling T1, approved by the owner 2026-10-09 ("D8 approve tooling"); catalogue-plan-v2
-- section 3.5 and critique finding F3 (scratchpad/session_2026-10-09-research-batch-24-
-- parameter-pilot/).
--
-- THE DEFECT. Migration 068 keyed `observed_terms` UNIQUE (ref_id, surface_form,
-- language), on the reasoning that "a second sighting of the same phrase in the same
-- source is the same fact", and `db.py observe-term` returned the earlier row with
-- `created: False` for any repeat. That holds for a phrase that names one thing. It is
-- false for a phrase a source uses for two quantities: the held ADA 2010 text says
-- "clear width" at a door clause and at a route clause (53 times across elements,
-- counted in the persisted HTML for the plan). The second sighting was folded into the
-- first, its locator and context quote were dropped, and the second sense was never
-- judged -- so the owner's requirement, "I expect harvesting across multiple terms if a
-- source discusses multiple terms" (2026-10-09), could not be met by the schema. Batch
-- 23's scanner had to invent an `also_at` field to carry the second place.
--
-- THE FIX. The sighting key gains the locator: UNIQUE (ref_id, surface_form, language,
-- COALESCE(locator, '')). Each sighting is judged on its own, so one sighting can name a
-- door width and another a corridor width. A deliberate second JUDGEMENT of one sighting
-- is unchanged: it is a second term_adjudications row, a contest (068's own design).
-- COALESCE because a NULL locator compares unequal to every other NULL, so without it
-- the legacy rows that carry no locator would stop deduplicating at all; with it they
-- keep exactly the old key. `observe-term` now refuses a NEW observation with no
-- locator, so the '' bucket holds only rows written before this migration.
--
-- A COPYING REBUILD, because SQLite cannot drop an inline table constraint. Same route
-- as 071 and 076: build, copy every row with its observation_id, drop, rename. The
-- inbound reference `term_adjudications.observation_id REFERENCES observed_terms` is
-- resolved by NAME at statement time, so it survives the rename; migrate_db.py hoists
-- `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` around the file and restores it after. No view or trigger
-- reads this table (checked against sqlite_master before writing this), so nothing has

-- SCHEMA migration — a record of each READING of a source, and the source-by-parameter
-- ledger derived from it. Tooling T1 (owner approval D8, 2026-10-09);
-- catalogue-plan-v2 section 3.8, critique finding F13.
--
-- THE GAP. Nothing recorded which source had been read for which parameter. A parameter
-- promoted in month three was never looked for in month one's sources, and the catalogue
-- could imply "no code sets a requirement" where nobody had read the code for that
-- quantity -- while every gate read green. That is how GAP-061's lost figures happened.
-- The owner's requirement it answers, 2026-10-09: "Ensure that we can add and expand
-- parameter catalogue as required based on new information we come across."
--
-- ONE ROW PER READING, NOT ONE ROW PER (SOURCE, PARAMETER). Parameter numbers are never
-- reused (base_parameters is AUTOINCREMENT, migration 076), so a reading that stores the
-- highest parameter_id existing when it was made says exactly which parameters it could
-- have covered: "catalogue version N" means "parameters 1..N, those active at the time".
-- Silence is then DERIVED by the view below; nobody writes an `absent` extraction for
-- every pair, and explicit `absent` rows stay for positive statements of absence.
--
-- `catalogue_version` IS COMPUTED BY THE WRITER, NEVER TYPED (CLAUDE.md rule 8):
-- `db.py record-scan` reads MAX(parameter_id) at call time and refuses a typed value.
-- `pages_read`/`pages_total` are computed the same way, from the page markers of the
-- file read (retrieval_log.page_coverage), and `file_sha256` must name a file the
-- retrieval-log manifests hold for this source. The CHECKs below hold the invariants for
-- every writer, including a data migration that does not go through db.py.
--
-- STAGE: evidence (governance/stage-map.yaml) -- what was read of an admitted source,
-- beside its extraction rows.
--
-- WHAT READS IT (CLAUDE.md section 8): `v_scan_ledger` below; the batch rule R16-scan in
-- scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py (every admission has a catalogue-mode reading);
-- scripts/audit/scan_debt.py through the view. Not built and not read here: a reading
-- does not prove the reader saw everything -- adversarial standing subject 4 samples
-- each source for figures no row carries.

CREATE TABLE source_scans (
    -- AUTOINCREMENT, as 076 did for the other ids a record names: a scan_id is cited by
    -- session records and must never come to mean a different reading.
    scan_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    ref_id              TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    -- catalogue: every active parameter up to catalogue_version.
    -- targeted:  one parameter, target_parameter_id (a back-fill reading).
    mode                TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (mode IN ('catalogue', 'targeted')),
    catalogue_version   INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (catalogue_version >= 1),
    target_parameter_id INTEGER REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),
    -- full: the whole document. partial: some pages of it. fragment: one page or clause
    -- of a larger instrument. abstract: an abstract or metadata record only.
    text_scope          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (text_scope IN
                                ('full', 'partial', 'fragment', 'abstract')),
    pages_read          INTEGER CHECK (pages_read IS NULL OR pages_read >= 0),
    pages_total         INTEGER CHECK (pages_total IS NULL OR pages_total >= 1),
    -- Which saved file was read, by checksum: the manifest's own sha256 of the bytes.
    file_sha256         TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (length(file_sha256) = 64),
    -- Whether the open pass (quantities the catalogue lacks, plan section 3.4) was done
    -- in this reading.
    open_pass_done      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (open_pass_done IN (0, 1)),
    -- full-read: the text was read against the list. pre-screen: only a script listed
    -- where catalogue terms occur -- weaker, and v_scan_ledger says which it was.
    method              TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('full-read', 'pre-screen')),
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT    NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT,
    CHECK ((mode = 'targeted' AND target_parameter_id IS NOT NULL)
        OR (mode = 'catalogue' AND target_parameter_id IS NULL)),
    CHECK (pages_read IS NULL OR pages_total IS NULL OR pages_read <= pages_total),
    -- "full" over a paged text means every page; a reading of fewer pages is partial.
    CHECK (text_scope <> 'full' OR pages_read IS NULL OR pages_read = pages_total)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_source_scans_ref ON source_scans(ref_id);

CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
--
-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
--   1 EXTRACTED          a non-absent extraction exists for the pair (any figure_role).
--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it.
--   5 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
-- A reading COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >=
-- parameter_id (the parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that
-- parameter. Rows 1 and 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence
-- than a reading recorded; 3 wins over 4 because a full reading supersedes a partial
-- one of the same source.
--
-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
WITH pairs AS (
    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id
      FROM evidence_sources e
     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
       AND p.status = 'active'
),
best AS (
    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id,
           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
                      s.scan_id DESC
             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
      FROM pairs pr
)
SELECT b.ref_id,
       b.parameter_id,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent') THEN 'EXTRACTED'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent') THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'
         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
       END AS status,
       b.scan_id,
       s.text_scope,
       s.method
  FROM best b
  LEFT JOIN source_scans s ON s.scan_id = b.scan_id;

"""
scripts/audit/scan_debt.py — which (source, parameter) pairs nobody has read in full?

WHY THIS EXISTS (tooling T1, 2026-10-09; catalogue-plan-v2 sections 3.8 and 8.2). The
owner's requirement: "Ensure that we can add and expand parameter catalogue as required
based on new information we come across." A parameter promoted in month three is owed a
look in month one's sources, and nothing showed that debt: the catalogue could imply "no
code sets a requirement" where nobody read the code for that quantity, while every gate
read green -- how GAP-061's figures were lost. `v_scan_ledger` (migration 103) derives a
status for every unsuperseded source x active parameter from the extractions and the
reading record (source_scans); this counts the pairs still owed.

DEBT = NOT-READ + READ-PARTIAL pairs. EXTRACTED, STATED-ABSENT and READ-NOTHING-FOUND are
accounted for. READ-PARTIAL is debt because a partial, fragment or abstract reading cannot
say a quantity is absent from the pages it did not see.

NO DEBT BASELINE, deliberately (the "no floor" this check was asked for). Debt RISES
legitimately -- every parameter promoted and every source admitted adds pairs -- so a
ratchet-down baseline would turn red on correct work. It is advisory and red whenever
debt > 0: the honest state of a catalogue that has not been read. Its readers: the next
cohort's worklist (the pairs printed below), the catalogue's evidence-state line, and the
Release 0 acceptance test (plan section 12, Q12), which will scope it to that source set.

EXAMINED is the number of ledger pairs. Zero pairs means no unsuperseded source or no
active parameter -- a corpus clear, which this project has done once (2026-09-13) -- and
the registry floor (min_items: 1) makes that visible rather than a silent pass.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/audit/scan_debt.py [--limit N]
Exit 0 no debt; 1 debt; 2 cannot run (no database, or a pre-103 schema).

import os

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/audit/observation_verbatim_audit.py — is each observation's quote in its source?

WHY THIS EXISTS (tooling T1, 2026-10-09; catalogue-plan-v2 section 8.2, critique F7).
An observation records that a source USES a phrase, with the sentence it sits in. Every
term and parameter the project mints comes from one. Until migration 102 nothing compared
that sentence with the source: the verbatim check had one call site, add-extraction. The
plan found that many of the observations then held verified only against another
source's file, or none (this audit prints the split). `db.py
observe-term` now refuses a new observation whose quote is not in its source's saved text
(or records an exemption); this is the BACKSTOP for the rows written before that, and for
any row arriving by another route (a data migration written by hand).

WHAT WRONG THING REACHES THE GUIDEBOOK WITHOUT IT (CLAUDE.md section 8): a vocabulary term
minted from a phrase the source never used, which no later gate can tell from a real one
-- the 2026-08-19 fabrication shape (CLAUDE.md 5(c)) one stage along. Its readers: R16
(every adjudicated observation names a disposed term) and the adversarial pass, which
reads the listed rows.

WHAT IT COUNTS, per observation, from retrieval_log.locate_quote (one matching rule):
  scoped    the quote is in a file saved FOR this ref_id               -- fine
  unscoped  only in another source's file (no structured ref_id)       -- counted
  missing   in no persisted, decodable artefact, or no quote at all    -- counted
  exempt    the row carries a recorded [VERBATIM-EXEMPT: reason]       -- reported
and REPORTS, separately, observations whose phrase is not inside their own quote.

RATCHET, NOT A FLOOR OF ZERO. The pre-102 debt cannot be repaired by this tooling PR (it
would be research rows, CLAUDE.md rule 10), so the two counted classes are compared with
`governance/research-contract-baseline.json` (keys observation-quote-missing and
observation-quote-unscoped). The check fails when either count EXCEEDS its baseline; a
count below it is debt paid, and the baseline is lowered in the PR that pays it. That
file's ratchet is witnessed by git (research_batch_dod.py --check-baseline, the blocking research_contract_baseline_ratchet), so the
numbers can only go down. Re-derive them by running this, never from a figure in prose.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/audit/observation_verbatim_audit.py
Exit 0 within baseline; 1 a count above baseline; 2 cannot run.
"""
import json
import os
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts" / "research"))
import retrieval_log                                                   # noqa: E402

DB_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", REPO / "data" / "guidebook.db"))
BASELINE_PATH = REPO / "governance" / "research-contract-baseline.json"
#: The two baselined classes, keyed as the baseline file names them.
KEYS = {"missing": "observation-quote-missing", "unscoped": "observation-quote-unscoped"}


def classify(conn):
    """[(observation_id, ref_id, kind, detail, phrase_inside_quote)] for every row."""
    return [(oid, ref) + retrieval_log.classify_observation(surface, quote, notes, ref)
            for oid, ref, surface, quote, notes in conn.execute(
                "SELECT observation_id, ref_id, surface_form, context_quote, notes "
                "FROM observed_terms ORDER BY observation_id")]


def main():
    if not DB_PATH.exists():
        print(f"observation_verbatim_audit: no database at {DB_PATH}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB_PATH}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    try:
        rows = classify(conn)
    finally:
        conn.close()
    base = {}
    if BASELINE_PATH.exists():
        base = json.loads(BASELINE_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("counts", {})

    by = {}
    for r in rows:
        by.setdefault(r[2], []).append(r)
    print("observation_verbatim_audit — is each observation's quote in its own source?")
    print(f"EXAMINED: {len(rows)}")
    for kind in ("scoped", "unscoped", "missing", "exempt"):
        print(f"  {kind:<9} {len(by.get(kind, []))}")
    outside = [r for r in rows if not r[4]]
    print(f"  REPORTED, not counted: {len(outside)} observation(s) whose phrase is not "
          f"inside its own quote: {[r[0] for r in outside][:20]}")
    if by.get("exempt"):
        print(f"  REPORTED, not counted: exempt observation(s) "
              f"{[r[0] for r in by['exempt']][:20]} -- the adversarial pass reads each "
              f"reason")

    over = []
    for kind, key in KEYS.items():
        n = len(by.get(kind, []))
        b = base.get(key)
        if b is None:
            over.append(f"{kind}: {n} with no baseline entry {key!r} in {BASELINE_PATH.name}")
        elif n > b:
            over.append(f"{kind}: {n} > baseline {b} ({key})")
            for oid, ref, _k, detail, _i in by[kind][:20]:
                print(f"    observation {oid} ({ref}): {detail[:160]}")
        elif n < b:
            print(f"  {kind}: {n} < baseline {b} -- debt paid down; lower {key} in "
                  f"{BASELINE_PATH.relative_to(REPO)} in this PR")
        else:
            print(f"  {kind}: {n} (baseline {b}) -- INHERITED DEBT, not a regression")
    if over:
        print("FAIL: " + "; ".join(over) + ". A new observation's quote must be in a file "
              "saved for its source (db.py observe-term refuses otherwise), so a rise means "
              "a row arrived by another route or an artefact was lost.")
        return 1
    print("PASS: no class above its baseline")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""
scripts/audit/extraction_follow_up_audit.py — open follow-ups, and live values resting on
one or on a skimmed figure.

WHY THIS EXISTS (tooling T1, 2026-10-09). The owner's answer to D1: "D1: yes figure from
source filed by another slug allowed. skimmed values are not publishable", read with the
earlier "should be yes, but we still tag it for follow up later" (ledger, "Owner
statements 2026-10-09"). So a figure read outside its source's admitting purpose MAY set a
published value while tagged (`db.py raise-follow-up`, extraction_follow_ups), and a
skimmed figure may NOT (dbcore.NOT_PUBLISHABLE_METHODS). This is the reader of both
answers.

WHAT IT DOES:
  * LISTS every open follow-up (extraction, source, parameter, reason, warrant).
  * FAILS a LIVE determination that has a GOVERNING link to an extraction with an open
    follow-up -- allowed by D1, but the reader must be told, and nothing renders that yet
    (catalogue-plan-v2 section 8.2, "follow-up governing"), so until the render states it
    this is the place it is said.
  * FAILS a live determination governed by a SKIMMED extraction -- the engine refuses to
    produce one, so this is the backstop for rows written by another route. K02 holds the
    same for a row re-marked skim after its determination was stamped.

VACUOUS TODAY, AND SAYS SO. No live determination exists and no follow-up has been raised
(both are counted below on every run), so it examines nothing until research raises the
first follow-up or the engine writes the first live determination. Registered with a
no_floor reason that asserts the subject is empty, so the run that finds a subject flags
that reason as stale -- the registry's own signal to ratchet the floor to min_items: 1.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/audit/extraction_follow_up_audit.py
Exit 0 nothing rests on an open follow-up or a skimmed figure; 1 something does;
2 cannot run.
"""
import os
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts"))
import dbcore                                                          # noqa: E402

DB_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", REPO / "data" / "guidebook.db"))


def main():
    if not DB_PATH.exists():
        print(f"extraction_follow_up_audit: no database at {DB_PATH}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB_PATH}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    try:
        if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='extraction_follow_ups'"
                            ).fetchone():
            print("extraction_follow_up_audit: extraction_follow_ups is absent "
                  "(pre-105 schema)", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        n_all = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM extraction_follow_ups").fetchone()[0]
        open_rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT f.follow_up_id, f.extraction_id, x.ref_id, x.parameter_id, f.reason, "
            "f.warrant, f.raised_by_session FROM extraction_follow_ups f "
            "JOIN source_value_extractions x ON x.extraction_id = f.extraction_id "
            "WHERE f.resolved_at IS NULL ORDER BY f.follow_up_id").fetchall()
        n_live = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM specifications "
                              "WHERE retired_at IS NULL").fetchone()[0]
        on_follow_up = conn.execute(
            "SELECT DISTINCT s.specification_id, l.extraction_id, f.follow_up_id "
            "FROM specifications s "
            "JOIN specification_extraction_links l ON l.specification_id = s.specification_id "
            "JOIN extraction_follow_ups f ON f.extraction_id = l.extraction_id "
            "WHERE s.retired_at IS NULL AND l.role = 'governing' AND f.resolved_at IS NULL "
            "ORDER BY 1, 2").fetchall()
        skim = dbcore.NOT_PUBLISHABLE_METHODS
        on_skim = conn.execute(
            "SELECT DISTINCT s.specification_id, l.extraction_id "
            "FROM specifications s "
            "JOIN specification_extraction_links l ON l.specification_id = s.specification_id "
            "JOIN source_value_extractions x ON x.extraction_id = l.extraction_id "
            "WHERE s.retired_at IS NULL AND l.role = 'governing' "
            f"AND x.extraction_method IN ({','.join('?' * len(skim))}) ORDER BY 1, 2",
            skim).fetchall()
    finally:
        conn.close()

    print("extraction_follow_up_audit — open follow-ups; live values resting on one")
    print(f"EXAMINED: {n_all + n_live}")
    print(f"  follow-ups: {n_all} raised, {len(open_rows)} open")
    for fid, eid, ref, pid, reason, warrant, by in open_rows[:50]:
        print(f"    follow-up {fid}: extraction {eid} ({ref}, parameter {pid}) {reason} -- "
              f"{warrant[:120]} [raised by {by}]")
    print(f"  live determinations: {n_live}"
          + ("" if n_live else " -- none exists, so the second half examines nothing"))
    bad = False
    for sid, eid, fid in on_follow_up:
        bad = True
        print(f"  FAIL: live determination {sid} is governed by extraction {eid}, which "
              f"has open follow-up {fid}. Allowed (owner D1, 2026-10-09), but the reader "
              f"must be told: state it on the render, or resolve the follow-up "
              f"(db.py resolve-follow-up).")
    for sid, eid in on_skim:
        bad = True
        print(f"  FAIL: live determination {sid} is governed by SKIMMED extraction {eid}. "
              f"Skimmed values are not publishable (owner 2026-10-09); re-run the engine "
              f"(scripts/assess/assess_cell.py) after retiring it.")
    if bad:
        return 1
    print("PASS: no live determination rests on an open follow-up or a skimmed figure")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

7557	def record_scan(data: dict, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
7558	    """Record one READING of one source against the parameter list (migration 103).
7559	
7560	    The scan contract (catalogue-plan-v2 section 3; owner 2026-10-09: "Slugs guide our
7561	    searches, but they do not guide what we derive and mine from sources!"): every
7562	    admitted source is read against the whole catalogue, and each reading leaves this
7563	    record, from which v_scan_ledger derives, for every (source, active parameter):
7564	    EXTRACTED, STATED-ABSENT, READ-NOTHING-FOUND, READ-PARTIAL or NOT-READ.
7565	
7566	    COMPUTED, NEVER TYPED (CLAUDE.md rule 8): `catalogue_version` is the highest
7567	    parameter_id at call time (ids are never reissued, so it says exactly which parameters
7568	    the reading could have covered), and pages read / pages total come from the file's
7569	    own page markers (retrieval_log.page_coverage) and, for a text derived from a PDF,
7570	    the PDF's page count.
7571	
7572	    REFUSES: a typed catalogue version; an unknown or superseded source (a tombstone is
7573	    never read again); a mode, scope or method outside the column's CHECK; a targeted
7574	    reading with no target, or a target that is not active; a catalogue reading when no
7575	    parameter exists; a --file-sha256 that is not a file the retrieval-log manifests hold
7576	    for this source, or whose bytes on disk no longer hash to it; `full` over a PDF (what
7577	    was read of a PDF is not knowable from the file: derive its text with
7578	    scripts/research/full_text.py and read that) and `full` over a text with fewer pages
7579	    than the document it was derived from.
7580	    """
7581	    if data.get("catalogue_version") is not None:
7582	        raise Refusal(
7583	            "record-scan: the catalogue version is COMPUTED, never typed -- it is the "
7584	            "highest parameter_id when the reading is recorded (CLAUDE.md rule 8). A typed "
7585	            "one could claim a reading covered parameters it never saw. Drop "
7586	            "--catalogue-version. Nothing was written.")
7587	    sha = (data.get("file_sha256") or "").strip().lower()
7588	    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", sha):
7589	        raise Refusal("record-scan: --file-sha256 must be the full sha256 (64 hex "
7590	                      "characters) of the saved file read, as the manifest records it.")
7591	    mode = data.get("mode")
7592	    target = data.get("target_parameter_id")
7593	    retrieval_log = _retrieval_log()
7594	    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
7595	        ref = dbcore.fold_ref(data.get("ref_id"))
7596	        src = conn.execute("SELECT ref_id, url FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id = ?",
7597	                           (ref,)).fetchone()
7598	        if src is None:
7599	            raise Refusal(f"record-scan: {data.get('ref_id')!r} is not an admitted source.")
7600	        _refuse_tombstone(conn, ref, "record-scan")
7601	        for col, flag in (("mode", "--mode"), ("text_scope", "--text-scope"),
7602	                          ("method", "--method")):
7603	            dbcore.check_declared(conn, "source_scans", col, data.get(col),
7604	                                  f"record-scan {flag}")
7605	        top = conn.execute("SELECT MAX(parameter_id) FROM base_parameters").fetchone()[0]
7606	        if top is None:
7607	            raise Refusal("record-scan: base_parameters holds no rows, so there is no "
7608	                          "catalogue to read a source against.")
7609	        if mode == "targeted":
7610	            if target is None:
7611	                raise Refusal("record-scan: --mode targeted needs --target-parameter-id, "
7612	                              "the one parameter this reading looked for.")
7613	            prow = conn.execute("SELECT status FROM base_parameters WHERE parameter_id = ?",
7614	                                (target,)).fetchone()
7615	            if prow is None or prow["status"] != "active":
7616	                raise Refusal(f"record-scan: --target-parameter-id {target} is "
7617	                              f"{'not a parameter' if prow is None else prow['status']}; a "
7618	                              f"reading is for an active parameter.")
7619	        elif target is not None:
7620	            raise Refusal("record-scan: --target-parameter-id is for --mode targeted; a "
7621	                          "catalogue reading covers every active parameter up to the "
7622	                          "catalogue version.")

7624	        match = [h for h in held if (h["sha256"] or "").lower() == sha]
7625	        if not match:
7626	            listed = "; ".join(f"{h['artefact']} {(h['sha256'] or '?')[:16]} ({h['via']})"
7627	                               for h in held) or "nothing"

7629	                f"record-scan: no file saved for {ref} has sha256 {sha[:16]}... The reading "
7630	                f"must name bytes the retrieval-log holds FOR this source. Saved for it: "
7631	                f"{listed}. Nothing was written.")
7632	        h = next((m for m in match if m["exists"]), match[0])
7633	        if not h["exists"]:
7634	            raise Refusal(f"record-scan: {h['session']}/{h['artefact']} is in the manifest "
7635	                          f"but not on disk. Nothing was written.")
7636	        import hashlib                                            # noqa: E402
7637	        if hashlib.sha256(h["path"].read_bytes()).hexdigest() != sha:
7638	            raise Refusal(f"record-scan: {h['session']}/{h['artefact']} no longer hashes "
7639	                          f"to its manifest sha256. Nothing was written.")
7640	        pages_read, pages_total = retrieval_log.page_coverage(h["path"])
7641	        if h["derived"] and h["derived_from"] and pages_read is not None:
7642	            sd, srec = retrieval_log.find_fetched_artefact(
7643	                h["derived_from"], prefer_dir=retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT / h["session"])
7644	            if srec is not None and srec["artefact"].lower().endswith(".pdf"):
7645	                held_pages = retrieval_log.pdf_page_count(sd / srec["artefact"])
7646	                if held_pages:
7647	                    pages_total = max(pages_total or 0, held_pages)
7648	        scope = data.get("text_scope")
7649	        if scope == "full":
7650	            if h["path"].suffix.lower() == ".pdf":
7651	                raise Refusal(
7652	                    f"record-scan: --text-scope full over a PDF ({h['artefact']}, "
7653	                    f"{pages_total or '?'} pages): what was read of a PDF is not knowable "
7654	                    f"from the file. Derive its text first -- python3 "
7655	                    f"scripts/research/full_text.py --ref-id {ref} --session {session} -- "
7656	                    f"and record the reading of that. Nothing was written.")
7657	            if pages_read is not None and pages_total and pages_read < pages_total:
7658	                raise Refusal(
7659	                    f"record-scan: --text-scope full, but {h['artefact']} carries "
7660	                    f"{pages_read} of {pages_total} pages. Record it as partial, or derive "
7661	                    f"every page (scripts/research/full_text.py) and read that. Nothing "
7662	                    f"was written.")
7663	        row = {"ref_id": ref, "mode": mode, "catalogue_version": top,
7664	               "target_parameter_id": target, "text_scope": scope,
7665	               "pages_read": pages_read, "pages_total": pages_total,
7666	               "file_sha256": sha, "open_pass_done": 1 if data.get("open_pass_done") else 0,
7667	               "method": data.get("method"),
7668	               "notes": (data.get("notes") or "").strip() or None}
7669	        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "source_scans", session))
7670	        cur = conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO source_scans ({','.join(row)}) "
7671	                           f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})", list(row.values()))
7672	        return {"scan_id": cur.lastrowid, "ref_id": ref, "catalogue_version": top,
7673	                "file": f"{h['session']}/{h['artefact']}", "pages_read": pages_read,
7674	                "pages_total": pages_total, "text_scope": scope, "dry_run": dry_run}

7677	def raise_follow_up(extraction_id: int, reason: str, warrant: str, session: str,
7678	                    dry_run: bool = False):
7679	    """Tag an extraction for a reviewer to re-check (migration 105).
7680	
7681	    The owner's D1 answer, 2026-10-09: a figure from a source filed under another slug may
7682	    set a published value, "but we still tag it for follow up later". Nothing can derive
7683	    that a figure was read outside the purpose its source was admitted for (no
7684	    slug-to-parameter map exists, and building one would be curation), so it is a
7685	    judgement with a required warrant. The plan's caution stands: under the scan contract
7686	    most whole-code figures are "from another slug", so tag only what a reviewer should
7687	    re-check against the parameter's own literature, and say why.
7688	
7689	    REFUSES: a reason outside the column's CHECK; a blank warrant; an unknown extraction;
7690	    a second OPEN follow-up for the same (extraction, reason), naming the open one.
7691	    """
7692	    warrant = (warrant or "").strip()
7693	    if not warrant:
7694	        raise Refusal("raise-follow-up: --warrant is required: what a reviewer should "
7695	                      "re-check, and why. A tag with no reason cannot be acted on.")
7696	    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
7697	        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "extraction_follow_ups", "reason", reason,
7698	                              "raise-follow-up --reason")
7699	        if not dbcore.exists(conn, "source_value_extractions", "extraction_id",
7700	                             extraction_id):
7701	            raise Refusal(f"raise-follow-up: extraction {extraction_id}: no such "
7702	                          f"extraction.")
7703	        prior = conn.execute(
7704	            "SELECT follow_up_id, raised_by_session FROM extraction_follow_ups "
7705	            "WHERE extraction_id = ? AND reason = ? AND resolved_at IS NULL",
7706	            (extraction_id, reason)).fetchone()
7707	        if prior:
7708	            raise Refusal(f"raise-follow-up: extraction {extraction_id} already has open "
7709	                          f"follow-up {prior[0]} ({reason}, raised by {prior[1]}). "
7710	                          f"Nothing was written.")
7711	        stamp = dbcore.now()
7712	        cur = conn.execute(
7713	            "INSERT INTO extraction_follow_ups (extraction_id, reason, warrant, raised_at, "
7714	            "raised_by_session) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
7715	            (extraction_id, reason, warrant, stamp, session))
7716	        return {"follow_up_id": cur.lastrowid, "extraction_id": extraction_id,
7717	                "reason": reason, "dry_run": dry_run}

6146	def observe_term(data: dict, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
6147	    """Record that a source USES a phrase. Makes no claim that it names our concept.
6148	
6149	    D-0173, the owner ruling this implements: "Recording that a source uses a phrase is
6150	    a fact about the document, not a claim that the phrase names one of our categories
6151	    -- the same epistemic act as recording its DOI."
6152	
6153	    So this writer accepts NO term_id, and there is no flag for one. Adjudication is a
6154	    different stage with its own writer. A single call that could observe and classify
6155	    at once would let the observation be born half-adjudicated, which is precisely the
6156	    presupposition the ruling exists to prevent.
6157	
6158	    ONE SIGHTING, NOT ONE PHRASE (migration 102, tooling T1, 2026-10-09). The key was
6159	    (ref_id, surface_form, language), so a phrase a source uses for two quantities --
6160	    the ADA's "clear width" at a door clause and at a route clause -- folded its second
6161	    sighting into the first and the second sense was never judged (critique F3). The key
6162	    is now the phrase AT A PLACE: a repeat of the same sighting still returns the earlier
6163	    row with `created: False`; the same phrase at another locator is a new observation.
6164	
6165	    A NEW OBSERVATION MUST BE VERIFIABLE (critique F7). The verbatim check had one call
6166	    site, add-extraction; observations -- the material every term and parameter is minted
6167	    from -- carried a quote nothing compared with the source. Many of the observations held
6168	    when this was written verified only against another source's text, or against none
6169	    (scripts/audit/observation_verbatim_audit.py derives the split). So a NEW observation
6170	    now requires --locator (the sighting's key)
6171	    and --context-quote; the phrase must occur inside its own quote; and the quote must be
6172	    found in a file saved FOR THIS SOURCE (retrieval_log.locate_quote, scoped by ref_id).
6173	    A hit only in another source's bytes is refused, not passed: it proves the words are
6174	    in the corpus, not that this source says them. `--verbatim-exempt <reason>` is the
6175	    recorded route for text no artefact of this source can carry (a page read from an
6176	    image, say), mirroring add-extraction: ledgered on the row's notes, and refused when
6177	    the quote DOES verify for this source. Rows written before migration 102 are not
6178	    re-checked here; scripts/audit/observation_verbatim_audit.py reports them.
6179	    """
6180	    surface = (data.get("surface_form") or "").strip()
6181	    if not surface:
6182	        raise Refusal("--surface-form is required: the phrase AS THE SOURCE WRITES IT.")
6183	    if "term_id" in data:
6184	        raise Refusal(
6185	            "observe-term does not accept a term_id. Observing that a source uses a "
6186	            "phrase is a fact about the document; deciding whether it names one of our "
6187	            "concepts is judgment, and belongs to `db.py adjudicate-term` (D-0173).")
6188	    locator = (data.get("locator") or "").strip() or None
6189	    quote = (data.get("context_quote") or "").strip() or None
6190	    exempt = (data.get("verbatim_exempt") or "").strip() or None
6191	    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
6192	        ref = dbcore.fold_ref(data.get("ref_id"))
6193	        if not dbcore.exists(conn, "evidence_sources", "ref_id", ref):
6194	            raise Refusal(
6195	                f"ref_id {data.get('ref_id')!r} is not an admitted source. A term is "
6196	                f"observed IN a source; observe it after the source is filed.")
6197	        _refuse_tombstone(conn, ref, "observe-term")
6198	        language = (data.get("language") or "EN").strip().upper()
6199	        prior = conn.execute(
6200	            "SELECT observation_id FROM observed_terms "
6201	            "WHERE ref_id=? AND surface_form=? AND language=? "
6202	            "AND COALESCE(locator, '') = COALESCE(?, '')",
6203	            (ref, surface, language, locator)).fetchone()

6205	            return {"observation_id": prior[0], "created": False,
6206	                    "reason": "this sighting -- the phrase at this locator in this "
6207	                              "source -- is already recorded"}
6208	        if not locator:
6209	            raise Refusal(
6210	                "observe-term: --locator is required for a new observation. An observation "
6211	                "is one SIGHTING, keyed on the phrase AND its place (migration 102); "
6212	                "without a place a second sense of the same phrase cannot be told from "
6213	                "the first. Give the clause, section or page as the source numbers it.")
6214	        if not quote:
6215	            raise Refusal(
6216	                "observe-term: --context-quote is required for a new observation: the "
6217	                "sentence the phrase sits in, verbatim, so judgment can adjudicate it and "
6218	                "the quote can be checked against the source's saved text (CLAUDE.md "
6219	                "5(c)).")
6220	        if not _retrieval_log().phrase_in_quote(surface, quote):
6221	            raise Refusal(
6222	                f"observe-term: --surface-form {surface!r} does not occur inside its own "
6223	                f"--context-quote. The quote is the sighting's evidence; a phrase that is "
6224	                f"not in it was not seen there. Nothing was written.")
6225	        marker = _require_scoped_verbatim(quote, ref, "--context-quote",
6226	                                          f"observe-term {ref}", exempt)
6227	        notes = (data.get("notes") or "").strip() or None
6228	        if marker:
6229	            notes = f"{notes} {marker}" if notes else marker

+    """(pages_read, pages_total) for a saved file, each None when it is not countable.

+    A derived text carrying `[PDF page N of M]` markers: pages_read is the number of
+    DISTINCT pages present, pages_total the largest M any marker states. A PDF: its page
+    count as the total, and pages_read None -- what was read of a PDF is not knowable from

+    text to be derived first. Anything else (a web page, an API record): (None, None).
+    """

def _refuse_live_work(conn, parameter_id, verb: str):
    """Refuse while a LIVE determination or an OPEN determination gate stands on it.

    A retirement or a merge changes what the parameter IS. A live determination was
    computed on it and would silently become a determination of a folded or abandoned
    subject; an open gate is a question about it that nobody could then answer. Retired
    determinations and resolved gates are history and do not block.
    """
    live = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT specification_id FROM specifications WHERE parameter_id = ? "
        "AND retired_at IS NULL ORDER BY 1", (parameter_id,))]
    if live:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{verb}: parameter {parameter_id} has LIVE determination(s) {live}. A "
            f"determination was computed on this parameter, and changing what the "
            f"parameter is would re-point it at a subject it was not computed for. Retire "
            f"each first (db.py retire-specification --specification-id N --reason ...), "
            f"then re-run this. Nothing was written.")
    gates = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT gate_id FROM determination_gates WHERE parameter_id = ? "
        "AND resolved_at IS NULL ORDER BY 1", (parameter_id,))]
    if gates:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{verb}: parameter {parameter_id} has OPEN determination gate(s) {gates}. "
            f"Resolve each with its rationale first (db.py resolve-determination-gate "
            f"--gate-id N --rationale ...): an open gate is a question about this "
            f"parameter that nobody could answer once it is retired or merged. Nothing was "
            f"written.")

## 2. CONFIRMED · HIGH · `mint-term-from-catalogue` accepts any name on any resolvable entry and any dated heading; the "approval" pointer proves nothing about the term

**Artifacts:** `scripts/db.py:7491-7493` ("APPROVE: a pointer to the ledger entry that records the owner's approval ... so the approval is mechanically tied to one recorded entry rather than asserted"), `:7522-7531`, `:7535-7552`; parser help `scripts/db.py:1912-1913` ("owner's approval quoted once in the ledger" — stale, it is a heading now); `scripts/validate_parameters.py:49-53`; `governance/check-registry.yaml:428-430`; `104:47-52`; ledger `references/project-standards.md` 2026-10-09 item 3 ("listed in one table, with the catalogue and the entry it came from, for the owner to approve before any is minted").

**Claim:** a catalogue-minted term carries the owner's recorded approval and the entry its name was taken from.

**Failure case:** neither pointer is compared with the name. On a scratch copy this wrote `TERM-095 'fixture handrail extension'` with `catalogue_entry_ref='ISO 21542:2011'` and `catalogue_approval_ref='Owner delegation 2026-10-14 — the simplification plan's §4 items ...'` — an entry that says nothing about handrails, a standard that was never read. Every refusal path passed: screened name, resolvable entry, dated heading occurring once. The "one table for the owner to approve" step has no mechanical form at all; P2 then re-checks only that the heading still occurs once.

Two more facts that make the entry pointer decorative:
- The owner's "Old corpus terms" catalogue is exhausted: all 88 `terms` in `_archived/data/corpus-pre-reset-2026-08-06.db` are already `canonical_en` of a live term (88 of 88, case-folded), so a mint from that catalogue with the catalogue's name is refused "already TERM-nnn", and the only name that gets through is one the catalogue does not contain (test M09 does exactly this: `canonical_en="fixture corpus term name"` from `terms:TERM-001`).
- For the registries, an entry is a `standard_cited` string (a standard's id), so "the name was taken from the entry" cannot be checked even in principle.

The rehearsal disclosed the weakening (`workplan/pipeline-state-graph/rehearsals/D-t1-landing-r25-r24.md:157`) and R25 was accepted by delegation (`RULINGS.md:316`, R49(e)), but the docstring, parser help, registry note and migration comment still state the stronger thing.
